lesson_evidence.heading: 1. Why eigenpairs matter
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$. A non-zero vector $v$ is an eigenvector if there is a scalar $\lambda$ such that

$$
Av=\lambda v.
$$

The scalar $\lambda$ is the corresponding eigenvalue. The vector must be non-zero: the zero vector satisfies this equation for every scalar and therefore gives no useful information about the action of $A$.

$$
A=Q\Lambda Q^T,

$$
